reviews.title: Excellent AI Technology, but Extremely Disappointing Customer Service
reviews.text:
I am changing my original review to one star.

The quality of HeyGen’s AI, avatars, and graphics is excellent. Unfortunately, the company’s customer service has been unacceptable.

I purchased the $100 Starter plan with the understanding that it included approximately $70 worth of credits each month. My previous creation and usage history appeared to support this because I was able to use more than 70 credits during earlier months. My expected credits were later stopped without a clear explanation.

I have sent multiple emails and submitted feedback through the app over several weeks. HeyGen has not responded to my emails, addressed my review, or provided any explanation regarding the original Starter plan.

I am simply asking HeyGen to review my original purchase agreement and account history. If monthly credits were included, they should be restored. If I misunderstood the plan, the company should provide the original written terms and explain exactly what I purchased. If HeyGen cannot honor the plan, I believe a fair refund or account credit should be offered.

The AI product may be impressive, but excellent technology does not make up for nonexistent customer service. Until someone responds and resolves this issue, I cannot recommend HeyGen.

reviews.title: misleading subscription system
reviews.text:
The weekly subscription is extremely misleading. I expected to pay for a week of access, but instead you receive limited credits, and every video generation or edit uses those credits.

Worse, the app itself created errors in my video, but I had to pay additional credits to try to fix errors I didn’t create. After just a couple of attempts, I ran out of credits and couldn’t properly edit the video.

The technology may be good, but the pricing model feels deceptive and makes the “weekly” subscription very frustrating to use.

reviews.title: £44.40 Wasted — Poor Results and No Response from Support
reviews.text:
Very poor results, no response from support, and a disappointing experience

I paid £44.40 for a HeyGen subscription, and the experience fell far short of their advertising. Whether I used a simple script or a carefully detailed one, the results were consistently disappointing.

I contacted support while creating my very first video, but nobody replied. I was left with poor results, no assistance, and the feeling that I had completely wasted my money.

I did not want to renew my subscription, yet another payment was attempted. Fortunately, I had already blocked further payments.

The whole experience left me feeling that collecting payments mattered more than providing a good service or looking after customers.

Do not rely on the adverts alone. Based on my experience, I would not recommend HeyGen at all.

reviews.title: AI avatar is cool BUT so many faults!
reviews.text: If I were just basing this on the video creation tools themselves then I would easily give this five stars. However, after paying $29 a month and getting 1200 credits, I attempted to make a video that cost 60 credits, ran into an error and lost the 60 credits anyway. I then proceeded to make two more videos for 60 credits of pop and those were successful. I then look at my remaining balance and I have 503 credit credits remaining. I’m missing 500+ credits in addition to the 60 that were due to a fault of the app. There’s absolutely no way to contact anyone via the app or desktop or any other means. So in my situation I’m just screwed basically and there’s no one there to fix it. I will not be renewing with them now or anytime in the future. Canceling is also a headache as you have to be on a desktop; you’re not able to cancel through the app or through the mobile site. I recommend that everyone steer clear. Such a shame because this app had a lot of potential.

reviews.title: Don’t waste your money here
reviews.text:
I used to really enjoy HeyGen, but the new credit system has made the app extremely disappointing and much too expensive for regular content creators.

Just a few days ago, some of my videos were costing around 18–24 credits to generate. Then similar videos started costing me 128 credits, and my most recent video used 227 credits. That is an enormous increase, especially when my monthly plan only includes a limited number of credits.

At this rate, the credits disappear after only a few videos, which makes the subscription almost useless for anyone who creates content regularly. I shouldn’t have to keep buying additional credits on top of an already paid subscription just to continue using the app.

The quality can be good, but the new pricing and credit system has completely changed the value of HeyGen. I really hope the company listens to its customers and either brings back a more affordable unlimited option or makes credit usage reasonable again.

Until this changes, I cannot recommend HeyGen to creators who need to make multiple videos each week.

reviews.title: Flaky product and customer service
reviews.text:
I subscribed to HeyGen’s $29/month Creator Plan to produce professional Enterprise AI educational videos. While the platform has useful capabilities, my experience was dominated by product defects and an exhausting support process.

Within days of subscribing, I encountered multiple issues:

• Walking Avatar generated an unnatural backward-and-forward motion, making two videos unusable.
• More than ten previously created photo avatars disappeared.
• Previously created Avatar Looks became unavailable on both the mobile app and desktop website.
• I lost more than 60 credits because of failed generations and an accidental generation while documenting the issue.
• Only 50 credits were restored.
• I later discovered an additional unexplained 40-credit discrepancy in my account.

The support team was polite and responded quickly, but every step required more work from me. I was repeatedly asked for screenshots, screen recordings, Google Drive uploads, video IDs, account verification, and requests to regenerate videos to prove the same defects. As a paying customer, I felt like I was performing quality assurance testing while consuming my own subscription credits.

The most frustrating part was that new issues kept appearing before previous ones were resolved. After the walking animation problem, my avatars disappeared. Then my Avatar Looks disappeared. Finally, I had to open another support case because my credit balance did not match the activity shown in my account.

For casual e

reviews.title: Unlimited Plan Removed – Subscription Cancelled
reviews.text:
I used to love this app and happily paid for the subscription because it allowed me to create as many videos as I needed. Unfortunately, the new credit system has completely ruined the value of the subscription. What was once an affordable monthly plan has turned into a constant upsell for more credits. I now run out of credits far too quickly, making the app much more expensive than before. Existing subscribers who signed up under the old pricing model feel punished instead of rewarded. The quality of the app is still good, but the new pricing makes it impossible to recommend.

After being a paying subscriber for over a year, I have now cancelled my subscription and will no longer use HeyGen. There are other alternatives that offer much better value for the money. Until the unlimited subscription option returns, I cannot recommend this app. Very disappointing.

reviews.text:
I get better results for free, unlimited, from Comfy UI running LTX2.3. This generated video that was supposed to be the person in the photo talking naturally behind a desk. The results look like EARLY ai. Lip sync? Decent. If more than the lips really moved other than a faint twitch it might be vaguely good. But he stayed ramrod stiff, hands and fingers never moved, it’s like a plastic mannequin had a talking face put on it. Tried other settings, other pictures… 

if you’re new to Ai and you’re like “wow, my picture is moving!” Ok yeah, it does that. If you want to use this to make “faceless” content where you have an Ai reading a script, prepare to have no followers. Anyone with a little bit of time and access to Claude to help set up comfy ui could figure out how to not have such basement-tier results. 

Much less the fact that if you use the web app and want to have API calls they’re not like the regular companies where when you subscribe, you can do that. Nope. Subscribe then pay a $10 fee on top of that because it’s the MINIMUM they accept to load your api wallet.

reviews.title: HeyGen’s New Update Ruined Realistic Avatars
reviews.text:
This new update honestly ruined the realism for me.

Before the update, the avatars felt subtle, elegant, natural, and cinematic. The movements were controlled and believable, especially for podcast-style or luxury content.

Now the facial expressions, eye movements, lip movements, and gestures are extremely exaggerated and over animated, even when using prompts requesting minimal motion and low expressiveness.

The avatars now feel cartoonish and unnatural instead of premium and realistic.

Please give creators more control over motion intensity, facial animation, gesture frequency, and expression levels, or bring back the older, more subtle animation style.

Right now it feels impossible to create calm, grounded, luxury-style content without the avatar overreacting constantly.

I paid for a month, made a few videos—very few—and then again they said I no longer had access to premium features and would need to purchase more credits.

In short, I don’t recommend it because you can’t fully use all the features even when you pay for a month. You might be able to use them once or twice, depending on what you’re doing.

reviews.title: 30 Dollars for a Paperweight—Zero Flexibility and Predatory Limits
reviews.text:
I am officially done with HeyGen. I signed up for the $30/month Creator plan to move forward with a professional film pitch, but the experience has been a total disaster.
First, the value is non-existent. I managed to get fewer than 20 short generations before hitting a credit wall. For a thirty-dollar monthly fee, that is an insulting amount of output. They heavily market 'unlimited' features, but anything actually usable (like high-fidelity avatars or premium motion) drains your tiny credit bucket instantly.
To make matters worse, when I tried to resolve the issue, I was told that upgrades and credit add-ons are 'not available in my area.' How can a global AI platform take my money for a subscription but then claim regional restrictions when I need to actually use the service I’m paying for? They have essentially bricked my account for the rest of the month with no path forward.
If you are a serious creator or a student on a deadline, stay far away. This isn't a tool; it's a dead end. I’ll be taking my workflow to D-ID or ElevenLabs where they actually value their customers' time and regional access.
Total waste of money.

reviews.title: Quality is dropping
reviews.text: I switched from Synthesia to Heygen a couple of years ago because Heygen made great strides in lip syncing with their avatars. Recently, however, I've had an impossible time getting avatars to speak naturally without unusual head or hand movements based on what's being said. I've tried both Avatar 3 and 4 and I'm not happy with the results. It doesn't matter what length of video you create. The problems don't seem to be able to be overcome.

I like the platform and the overall idea behind it, but the credit system needs serious improvement.

Credits get consumed very quickly, even when the issue is caused by the AI itself. For example, when the output has errors, glitches, or doesn’t follow the instructions correctly, you still lose full credits. This makes the process frustrating and expensive, especially when you need to regenerate content multiple times.

It would be much more fair if users were not charged for results that are clearly flawed or unusable. A refund or retry system for failed generations would greatly improve the experience.

The tool has a lot of potential, but the current credit system makes it difficult to use consistently and confidently.

reviews.title: WARNING: False Advertising. "Unlimited Videos" is a Deceptive Bait-and-Switch.
reviews.text:
I signed up for the $29/month Creator plan specifically because it advertised as providing “Unlimited Avatar Videos”. This promise is completely false and severely misleading. 

The core, high-quality feature the company advertises is not unlimited at all. The paid creator plan gives you only 10 minutes of Avatar IV credits per month. I ran out of credits after creating just a few short videos, effectively crippling the service and making it unusable for serious business content creation, I was not even able to finish a complete video.

When I emailed Support, they confirmed this restriction and stated that the high-quality feature is intentionally metered and pointed me to an obscure FAQ page after I had already purchased the plan. This is a classic bait and switch tactic: the advertise unlimited to get you to sign up, but restrict the one feature you actually want.

If you rely on the latest, most realistic avatars for your work, I personally would not trust the “unlimited” claim. You’ll be forced to either use their previous models or pay extensive add-on fees after just a few minutes of video.
